solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mineral is yellow — the coal's different

indicators.note: making something different means changing its make-up, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow
taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A geologist notes that a yellowish mineral differs from the coal beside it.
explanation.walkthrough: Heraldic OR for yellow is a crossword staple; the rest is a rearrangement of THE COAL'S, giving ORTHOCLASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthoclase is a common potassium feldspar, a rock-forming mineral found in granite.

clue.text: Traveller getting round — movement restored?

blocks.note: a Rom is a Romany, a traveller
the round letter

explanation.surface: A traveller circling about wonders whether some movement has been brought back.
explanation.walkthrough: ROMO was the 1990s revival of the New Romantic pop movement, hence 'restored?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Romo was a short-lived music-press label for a revival of the New Romantic style, a movement brought back.

clue.text: Like a terrible accident with smoke going up after short time

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, backwards

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a cigar is something to smoke

explanation.surface: An accident scene with smoke rising shortly afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the upturned smoke beneath T in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrible accident causing great loss or suffering is described as tragic.

clue.text: Poor performers cramping a political organisation

indicators.note: cramping means squeezing something in, so the outer word holds another inside it

blocks.note: hams are bad, over-the-top actors
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bad actors are said to be hampering some political group.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamas is the Palestinian Islamist movement with a political wing, a political organisation.

clue.text: Crowd about to descend with great desire and little hesitation

blocks.note: C is short for circa, about
lust is strong desire
er is the short sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A crowd is about to come down, full of eagerness and barely hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, the pieces after C 'descend' below it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cluster is to gather closely together, to crowd.

clue.text: Crazy old army officer shown up

indicators.note: in a down entry, shown up means presented from the bottom upward, so back to front

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
Col is short for colonel

explanation.surface: An elderly, unhinged colonel is exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Loco is slang, from Spanish, for mad or crazy.

clue.text: A rogue uncle once in the world of learning

blocks.note: taken as written
a cad is a dishonourable man
eme is an old word for an uncle

explanation.surface: A disreputable former uncle turns out to be an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks EME as obsolete, a Scots and archaic word for uncle.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the academic community and its environment, the sphere of scholarship.

clue.text: Once like ABC (part of alphabet here)?

indicators.note: part of means only a piece of the following words is taken, inside them

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Is the start of the alphabet simple, as people used to say?
explanation.walkthrough: ETHE is an archaic word meaning easy, as easy as ABC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethe is an obsolete form meaning easy, and something as easy as ABC is simple.

clue.text: Nest is arranged for offspring, as before

indicators.note: arranged means set out in some new order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A nest is prepared for the young birds, as previously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks an obsolete word: Spenser's SIENT is a scion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sient is the Spenserian spelling of scion, a descendant, so the plural means offspring.

clue.text: Homeless, so tent there may provide the answer

indicators.note: a set of letters that may provide the answer is raw material, to be reordered into the solution

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: For someone without a home, a tent pitched there might be the solution.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living on the street has no home, so the phrase means homeless.

clue.text: Soldiers in a crisis sure having to scatter

indicators.note: to scatter is to disperse in all directions, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Troops caught in an emergency are bound to disperse.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuirassiers were cavalry soldiers who wore a cuirass, a breastplate.

clue.text: Ingots perhaps hard to get out, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear signals that the wordplay works by sound rather than by spelling

blocks.note: someone blocked in finds it hard to get out

explanation.surface: Are bars of metal difficult to extract, apparently?
explanation.definitionFit: Block tin is pure tin cast into blocks or ingots, so ingots are an example.

clue.text: Greek character going round with French pal, showing taste

indicators.note: going round means turning about, so the letter's name is read backwards

blocks.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A Greek touring with a French friend shows good taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Umami is the savoury fifth basic taste, alongside sweet, sour, salt and bitter.

clue.text: Prestige of court blown apart by a revolutionary

indicators.note: something blown apart has a gap opened in it, so the outer word is split to take others inside

blocks.note: Ct is the abbreviation for court
taken as written
Che Guevara, the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A court's standing is shattered by a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachet is distinction or prestige, the quality of being admired.

clue.text: Old schools. Old-fashioned characters

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: Former schools are recalled alongside an outdated alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schools' looks educational but means groups of whales, GAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogam, or ogham, is the ancient Irish alphabet, so its letters are old characters.

clue.text: Censure mother and children ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: a dam is an animal's mother
the final letter

explanation.surface: A mother scolds her children in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To damn is to condemn or criticise severely, a synonym of censure.

clue.text: Jittery trainee hates to take more chances early on

indicators.note: jittery means nervous and shaking, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A nervous novice dislikes taking bigger risks at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: In poker the ante is the stake put in before the deal, so raising it ups the risk at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to increase the stakes, and the ante is staked before play begins.

clue.text: Gun that is placed by bridge

blocks.note: an arch spans a gap, a bridge
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A firearm is set down beside a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: ARCHIE was First World War slang for an anti-aircraft gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Archie was the airmen's nickname for an anti-aircraft gun and its fire.

clue.text: Part of leg, not head, in a restraining hold

indicators.note: not head means the leading letter is removed

blocks.note: the shank is the lower leg

explanation.surface: A wrestler grips the lower leg without the head in a hold.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots and dialect a hank is a hold or grip, a restraining influence over someone.

clue.text: Pattern on window, maybe — what could be finer around church?

indicators.note: what could be signals a word that could become something else when its letters are reordered
around means surrounding, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A frost picture on a church window: what could look finer?
explanation.definitionFit: Ice fern is the fern-like frost pattern that forms on window glass in winter.

clue.text: Period of detention brings strain to holy type

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for saint
to retch is to strain as if vomiting

explanation.surface: A spell in custody puts stress on a pious person.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious synonym for strain is the answer itself; here strain means retch.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch is informal for a prison sentence, a term served inside.

clue.text: Confusion of small son, tot in a spin

indicators.note: something in a spin is turning round, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: S abbreviates both small and son
to tot up is to add, so a tot is a sum

explanation.surface: A little boy and a toddler whirl about in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A muss is a state of disorder or mess, a muddle.

clue.text: Part of tennis match concluded by ace — it's hairy

definitions.note: a phrase describing the answer, a bristle

blocks.note: a tennis match is divided into sets
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A set finished with an ace makes for a hairy moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairy' looks like slang for dangerous, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A seta is a bristle or hair-like structure in zoology and botany.

clue.text: Stored in pocket, a long optical device

indicators.note: stored in means kept inside, so the letters lie within the next words

blocks.note: running across the end of the first word into the next two

explanation.surface: A long instrument is kept in a pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: An étalon is an interferometer of two parallel reflecting plates, used in optics.

clue.text: Number given to worker who may be temporary resident

blocks.note: ten is a number
the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A figure is assigned to an employee who might be a short-term lodger.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant occupies property rented from a landlord, often for a limited term.

clue.text: Aim to be quiet when anger spreads around

indicators.note: something spreading around surrounds what lies inside it

blocks.note: as can mean when
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Try to keep calm as rage spreads.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to aim at or hope to achieve something.

clue.text: Mason restores ends getting broken

indicators.note: getting broken means being smashed apart, so the letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A builder repairs broken ends of stonework.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone dresser shapes and finishes stone, a mason's work.

clue.text: Sage's farewell cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter is lopped off

blocks.note: so long is a goodbye

explanation.surface: A wise man's goodbye is curtailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Solon was the Athenian lawgiver, and his name is used for any wise statesman.

clue.text: Glasgow's empty grave being reported

indicators.note: something reported is spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a tomb is a grave

explanation.surface: A deserted burial place in Glasgow is in the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Toom is the Scots word for empty.

clue.text: Fighting female, adult repeatedly seen among ladies?

indicators.note: seen among means placed within something, so letters go inside

blocks.note: the ladies is a lavatory, a WC
A for adult, twice

explanation.surface: A combative woman, with grown-ups showing up again and again in the ladies' toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: The WAAC was the Women's Army Auxiliary Corps of the First World War, and a member was called a Waac.
explanation.definitionFit: A Waac was a woman serving in the British army auxiliary corps, a female in the forces.

clue.text: Fish hangs loosely on end of line

indicators.note: end of means only the last letter of the following word is used

blocks.note: the final letter
to lop is to hang down limply

explanation.surface: A fish dangles slackly at the end of a fishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: Elops is a genus of tarpon-like fish, the ladyfish.

clue.text: Some words needing to be cut, as before

indicators.note: some means just a portion of the following words is taken

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Certain words need trimming, as previously.
explanation.definitionFit: Snee is given in Chambers as an obsolete word for to cut, so the old usage fits.

clue.text: Weed in open ditch running into river

indicators.note: running into means flowing inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: ea is a dialect word for a river or running water
a lode is an open ditch or watercourse in the Fens

explanation.surface: Weeds grow in a ditch that drains into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Elodea is a genus of aquatic plants, the pondweed often called Canadian waterweed.

clue.text: Gradation of differences in Conservative policy

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: Tory policy shows shades of variation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cline is a continuous gradient of variation within a species or between categories.

clue.text: Description of bar Jock's eager to provide for car attachment

blocks.note: a roo bar is the guard on a vehicle's front, so roo describes the bar
frack is a Scots word for eager or ready

explanation.surface: A Scotsman in a pub is eager to describe a car accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but it is a roo bar, a kangaroo guard fitted to a vehicle's front; 'Jock' is a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof rack is a frame fixed on a car's top to carry luggage.

clue.text: Tree — prominent feature on isle, something slippery

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing on another is placed after it, so the second-named piece comes first

blocks.note: the Isle of Man
the chin is a prominent part of the face
eels are proverbially slippery

explanation.surface: A tree stands out on an island where eels slither.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is the usual crossword isle; a facial feature placed on it comes after it in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The manchineel is a highly poisonous Caribbean tree with milky sap.
